in_greek.name: Ζανέττα
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Ζανέττα προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν ἑλληνικὴ λέξη 'χάρις', ἡ ὁποία σημαίνει 'χάρις' ἢ 'εὐμένεια'. Ἐκφράζει τὴν εὐμένεια καὶ τὸ ἔλεος τοῦ Θεοῦ, καθὼς καὶ τὴν πίστιν στὴν εὐεργεσία τοῦ Θεοῦ.

in_latin.name: Zanetta

She was born in Mantua, Italy, and was a member of the powerful and influential Gonzaga family. Zanetta was known for her beauty, intelligence, and charm, and was an influential figure in the Medici court. She was a patron of the arts and supported such artists as Galileo Galilei and Michelangelo.

Zanetta Fonseca (1460-1538) was a Portuguese noblewoman who was the mother of King Manuel I of Portugal. She was the daughter of the Count of Baraçal and was married to Afonso, Duke of Braganza. Zanetta was known for her piety and her support of the Jesuit order. She played an important role in the politics of the Portuguese court during the reign of her son, and was an influential figure in the spread of the Jesuit order throughout Portugal and its colonies.
